86:1: Our Lord swears by the sky and by the night-comer who knocks at night from the shining stars, and is hidden during the day, and everything that comes at night has knocked. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the sky and the night-comer. He said: The sky and what is knocked on in it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “By the sky and the nightcomer. And what can make you know what is the nightcomer?” He said: A nightcomer who knocks at night and is hidden during the day. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the night visitor, he said: The appearance of the stars, meaning: He visits you at night. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Night-Taker, that it means the star.
86:2: God Almighty says: And what will make you know what is the Nightcomer? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: What makes you know, O Muhammad, what is the Nightcomer by which you swore? Then He, may His praise be glorified, explained that, saying: It is the piercing star, meaning: Its light is blazing and glowing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
86:3: Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, the piercing star, meaning: the shining one. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The piercing star he said: It is the shining planets, and its holes: if it shines. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, the piercing star, he said: the one that pierces. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, The Piercing, he said: The one who glows. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: His light. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The piercing star means the shining one. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, The piercing star, he said: The Arabs used to call the Pleiades the star, and it is said that the piercing star is the star that is called Saturn, and the piercing star is also: that which has risen above the stars, and the Arabs say to a bird when it has reached the belly of the sky high: it has pierced, and the Arabs say: pierce your fire, meaning light it up.
86:4: And his saying: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. Among the reciters of Medina, Abu Ja`far recited it, and among the reciters of Kufa, Hamza, for it has with emphasis. It was reported from Al-Hasan that he recited it likewise. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Abu Ubaid told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to read it: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it with emphasis, and he would say: except for a guardian over it. And this is how everything in the Qur’an is with emphasis. And Nafi’ from the people of Madinah read it, and Abu Amr from the people of Basra read it: lama with emphasis, meaning: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it. And the lam is the answer to in and ma that comes after it is a connection, and if that is the case then there is no emphasis in it. And the reading that I do not choose other than that is: the lightening, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, and a group of people who know the speech of the Arabs denied the emphasis, that it is known from the speech of the Arabs, except that Al-Farraa used to say: We do not know the reason for the emphasis in that, and we see that it is a language of Hudhayl, they make except with the lightened in for what, and they do not go beyond that, as if he said: There is no soul but that it has a guardian, so if what Al-Farraa mentioned is correct, that it is the language of Hudhayl, then reading it is correct and unjust, even if the choice is also the other reading, if that is correct with us, which is the lightening, because that is the well-known speech of the Arabs, and the more familiar should not be abandoned for the more unknown. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Abu Ubaid told us, he said: Muadh told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said: I read to Ibn Sirin, Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it, and he denied it and said, Glory be to God, glory be to God. The interpretation of this statement is that every soul has a guardian from its Lord, who records its deeds and records what it earns of good or evil. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it, he said: Every soul has guardians over it from among the angels. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it: Guardians who guard your deeds, your provision, and your lifespan when you take it, O son of Adam, you will be taken to your Lord.
86:5: And His statement: So let man consider from what he was created. God Almighty says: So let man consider who denies resurrection after death, who denies God’s ability to revive him after his death. From what he was created. He says: From what did his Lord create him?
86:6: Then He, the Most High, informed us of what He created him from, saying: He was created from gushing water, meaning from gushing water. This is one of the things that the Arabs used to use as a verb, which means the passive participle. It is said that most of those who use this among the living Arabs are the inhabitants of the Hijaz, if it is in the manner of description, like their saying: This is a hidden secret, which is a verbal noun, and so on.
86:7: And his saying: It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs means: It comes out from between that, and the meaning of the words is from them, just as it is said: Much good will come out from between these two things, meaning: It comes out from them. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the collarbones and their location. Some of them said: The collarbones are the location of the necklace on a woman’s chest. Who said that? Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad Al-Tafawi told me: Muhammad bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Sabur, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The backbone and the collarbones. He said: The collarbones are the place of the necklace. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, It comes forth from between the backbone and the ribs, meaning: from between the breasts of the woman. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: Ikrimah was asked about the collarbones, and he said: These, and he placed his hand on his chest between his breasts. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Salma bin Qutaybah told me, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Nu’man Al-Hadani told me that he heard Ikrimah say: It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs. He said: The backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The collarbones are the chest. He said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Misa’ar, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, who said: The collarbones are the chest. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Hab told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs, he said: The ribs are the chest, and this is the backbone, and he pointed to his back. Others said: The collarbones are the area between the shoulders and the chest. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The collarbones are what is between the shoulders and the chest. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the collarbones, he said: lower than the collarbones. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: The back is for the man, and the collarbones are for the woman, and the collarbones are above the breasts. Others said: It is the hands, the feet, and the eyes. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. He said: The ribs are the extremities of the man, the hands, the feet, and the eyes. Those are the ribs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs. He said: The ribs are the hands and feet. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Someone else said: The collarbones are the woman’s semen and the man’s loins. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs: His eyes, his hands, and his feet. Others said: The meaning of this is that it comes out from between the man’s loins and throat. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, It comes out from between the backbone and the ribs, meaning: It comes out from between the man’s backbone and his throat. Others said: They are the ribs below the backbone. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ashhath, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, regarding his statement, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs, he said: The ribs are the ribs below the backbone. Others said: It is the essence of the heart. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Al-Layth told me that Muammar bin Abi Habeeba Al-Madani told him that he had heard about the statement of God, It emerges from between the backbone and the ribs, he said: It is the juice of the heart, and from it comes the child. The correct statement regarding this matter, in our view, is the statement of those who say: It is the place where the necklace falls on a woman’s chest, because that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs, and it is what their poetry came from. Al-Muthaqab Al-Abdi said: And gold is made on a smooth ivory-colored, soft, and delicate surface. Another said: And saffron on her collarbones, eastward, with its pearls and its throat
86:8: And His statement: Indeed, He is Able to gather it together God Almighty says: Indeed, He who created you, O people, from this gushing water, and made you into well-proportioned human beings, after you were gushing water, is Able to return it. The people of interpretation differed regarding the letter ha’ in His statement, upon his return, as to what it refers to. Some of them said: It refers to the water, and they said: The meaning of the statement is: God is able to return the sperm to the place from which it came out. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, Indeed, He is able to bring him back, he said: He is able to return him to his loins. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement, Indeed, He is Able to bring him back, he said: To the crucifixion. Ubaid bin Ismail Al-Habbari told me: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, He is Able to return it, he said: To return the water to the urethra. Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi Al-Washa’ told me: Abu Qatn Amr bin Al-Haitham told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, He is Able to return it, he said: To return the sperm to the urethra. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, He is Able to return him, he said: in the urethra. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: He is able to return him. He said: He returned him to the urethra. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that it is about returning man to water as he was before He created him from it. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Indeed, He is Able to bring him back, if you wish, you can return him as You created him from water. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that He is able to hold back that water. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, He is Able to return it, he said: He is Able to return that water, so that it does not come out, just as He was able to create from it what He created, He is Able to return it. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that He is able to return a person from a state of adulthood to a state of youth. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Husayn told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: I heard him say regarding His statement, Indeed, He is Able to return him, that he said: If you wish, You can return him from old age to youth, and from youth to childhood, and from childhood to sperm. According to this interpretation, the ha in His statement, on his return is from the male human being. Others who claimed that the letter ha refers to man said: The meaning of this is that He is able to revive him after his death. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, He is Able to bring him back, God Almighty mentioned that He is Able to resurrect him and bring him back. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said that the meaning of this is: God is able to restore the human being created from gushing water after his death to life as he was before his death. I said that this is the most correct of the sayings on that, because of His saying, On the Day when secrets will be exposed, so in following it with His saying, He is able to bring him back, there was report of the Resurrection, indicating that what preceded it was also from it, On the Day when secrets will be exposed, God Almighty says: He is able to revive him after his death, on the Day when secrets will be exposed, so the Day is from the description of the return, because the meaning is: He is able to bring him back on the Day when secrets will be exposed.
86:9: What he meant by his saying: The Day when secrets will be exposed is the day when the secrets of the servants will be tested, and on that day what was hidden from the eyes of the servants in this world will be revealed, of the obligations that God had imposed upon him and commanded him to perform. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Saleh, on the authority of Yahya bin Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, regarding his statement, On the Day when secrets will be exposed, he said: That is fasting, prayer, and ritual bathing for major ritual impurity, which are the secrets. If he had wanted to, he could have said, I fasted but I am not fasting, “I prayed but he did not pray,” I bathed but he did not bathe. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, On the Day when secrets will be exposed, these secrets will be tested, so conceal goodness and announce it if you are able, and there is no power except with God. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, On the Day when secrets will be exposed, he said: They will be tested.
86:10: And His statement: So he will have no power or helper. God Almighty says: On that Day, the disbelieving human will have no power to protect himself from God's punishment and painful torment, nor will he have any helper to aid him or rescue him from whoever has harmed him. In this world, he would have recourse to a force from his clan, with whom he could protect himself from whoever wanted to harm him, and a helper from an ally who would aid him against whoever wronged and oppressed him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, For he has no power or helper means that God will help him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, nor any helper, he said: No strength by which to protect himself, nor any helper to aid him from God. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, regarding his statement, Neither strength nor helper, he said: Strength is the clan, and helper is the ally.
86:11: God Almighty says: And the sky full of paths meaning the paths of clouds and the provisions of the servants every year. From this is what Al-Mutanakhal said in describing Saif: White as a sediment, if it does not settle in a party, it will be alone And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the sky with its paths he said: The clouds in which there is rain. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Muammil told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the sky with its paths, he said: with its clouds in which there is rain. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the sky with its rains meaning: by rains: the rain and sustenance every year. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And the sky full of returns, he said: It returns with people’s provisions every year. Abu Raja’ said: Ikrimah was asked about it, and he said: It returns with the rain. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of the return, he said: The clouds rain, then return with the rain. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the sky full of returns, he said: It returns with the provisions of the servants every year. Were it not for that, they would perish, and their livestock would perish. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the sky full of returns, he said: It returns with rain every year. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the sky full of paths, meaning the rain. Others said: What he means by that is that its sun and moon set and rise. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the heaven with its paths, he said: Its sun, moon, and stars come from here.
86:12: And His saying: And the land with its fissures, God Almighty says: And the land with its fissures with plants. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the land with its cracks, he said: with its plants. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the earth with its fissures, meaning: Its fissures produce plants every year. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And the earth with its cracks, he said: This cracks open from what is beneath it. Abu Raja’ said: Ikrimah was asked about it, and he said: This cracks open from the provision. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the land with its cracks like the Ma’zam, the Ma’zam of Mina. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the land with its fissures. He said: The fissure is like a narrow passage, not valleys or cliffs. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the earth with its cracks, it cracks open to produce fruits and plants, as you have seen. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the earth with its cracks. He said: It cracks open to produce plants. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And the earth with its fissures, and he recited, Then We split the earth with a fissure, and produced therein grain, and grapes and herbage (Abasa 80:26-28) to the end of the verse, he said: He split it for cultivation. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the earth with its cracks, meaning the plants.
86:13: And His statement: Indeed, it is a decisive statement. God Almighty says: Indeed, this statement and this report are a decisive statement. He says: It is a statement that distinguishes between truth and falsehood with its clarification. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with differences among them in their expression of it. Some of them said: for a true statement. Some of them said: To say a ruling. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed, it is a decisive statement, meaning: true. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, it is a decisive statement: meaning a ruling.
86:14: And his saying: And it is not a joke means: It is not a game or falsehood. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And it is not a joke, meaning: falsehood. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And it is not a joke, he said: a game.
86:15: God Almighty says: Indeed, they are plotting a plot. God Almighty says: Indeed, these people who deny God, His Messenger, the promise, and the threat are plotting a plot.
86:16: And His saying: And He certainly planned a plan, means: And He planned a plan, and the plan He, may His praise be glorified, planned for them is His dictation of them to disobey Him and disbelieve in Him.
86:17: And His statement: So give the disbelievers respite. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So give the disbelievers respite, O Muhammad, and do not be hasty with them. Give them respite for a little while. He says: Give them respite for a short time, and give them respite until the appointed time, which is the time when the punishment will befall them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Give them respite for a while, meaning: soon. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Give them respite for a while. Respite means a little. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “So give the disbelievers respite. Give them respite for a while.” He said: Give them respite, so do not rush them and leave them alone, until when he wanted to take revenge on them, he ordered him to fight them and fight them, and to be harsh with them.
